Proszowice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Proszowice, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Proszowice developed through the 19th century; by 1921, 1,307 (39.6%) grew to about 2,500 during wartime refugee influxes, mostly murdered at Bełżec in 1942. This cemetery, probably established in the 19th century, was fenced with a wall in the 1930s; Germans used some matzevot to reinforce the Szreniawa River's banks during WWII. Poland formally closed the cemetery in January 1971 following a 1970 municipal resolution; an unnamed US citizen funded fencing before 1983, and Zygmunt Just (Juskiewicz) of Mannheim led further restoration in the late 1980s. A 2012 granite Holocaust memorial stele was unveiled at the site. Only 65 Jews returned to Proszowice in 1945, soon leaving after suffering attacks.
